Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.

src_text: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. src_text: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)

src_text: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. His stunning knock of 150 off 148 balls, laced with 11 fours and five sixes, surpassed the previous record held by the legendary West Indies' batter Desmond Haynes, who scored 148 in his maiden ODI innings against Australia back in 1978. Before Breetzke's innings, the highest score on ODI debut for South Africa was 124 by Colin Ingram against Zimbabwe in 2010. Now, Breetzke stands alone at the top, delivering a performance that showcased patience, aggression, and remarkable shot selection as South Africa posted a mammoth 304/6.

Tema vapustav 150 punkti löök 148 pallist, kus oli 11 nelikku ja viis kuusikut, ületas eelmise rekordi, mida hoidis legendaarne Kariibi mere piirkonna mängija Desmond Haynes, kes sai 148 punkti oma esimeses ODI mängus Austraalia vastu aastal 1978. src_text: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
target_text: Film „Nosferatu: Symfonie hrůzy“ od F. W. Murnaua je sám o sobě remake – neautorizovaná adaptace románu „Drákula“ od Brama Stokera, což je naprosto fascinující a zároveň děsivý příběh – a Murnau spolu se scenáristou Henrikem Galeenem si zachovali mnoho z toho, co bylo na původním díle tak působivé, a zároveň do něj vnesli své vlastní významné změny. Například oni jsou zodpovědní za tradici, která se pevně zakořenila, a to, že sluneční světlo může zničit upíra, což se v knize Stokera vůbec nevyskytuje. Pravděpodobně jsem „Nosferatu“ viděl v příliš mladém věku. Bylo mi šest let, televize PBS vysílala takové věci a moje chůva byla ráda, že jsem nezapálil dům. Ale i tak by mě to film naprosto ohromil, kdybych ho viděl v jakémkoli věku. Bylo to, jako bych cítil chlad z hrobu. (Jeho dopad byl tak trvalý, že o 30 let později jsem napsal román inspirovaný tímto filmem a jeho vznikem.) Celý film nebyl tolik děsivý, jako spíše znepokojivý a podvratný, a to všechno začalo postavou Nosferata. Výkon Maxe Schrecka je i 102 let po natočení filmu stále měřítkem pro zlověstnou a důstojnou odpudivost. Upír, kterého ztvárnil Schreck, má klid a nehybnost postavy ve špatném snu nebo pavouka ve své síti, a svět, ve kterém žije, je v mnoha ohledech stejně znepokojivý. Po první děsivé noci hrdiny, Huttera, v zámku Nosferata si všimne v zrcadle, že ho něco pokousalo do krku, a on se usměje.

Why is even on the iPhone 1 an empty key? Why did USA get +1?
The old Bell network had 1 reserved as a shortcut to the long distance network! So if a town started with the letters ABC you’d… yes automatically get onto the long distance network, at a heavy charge. Thus this separation!

Perché anche sull'iPhone 1 c'è una chiave vuota? Perché gli Stati Uniti hanno ottenuto il +1?

src_text: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. His stunning knock of 150 off 148 balls, laced with 11 fours and five sixes, surpassed the previous record held by the legendary West Indies' batter Desmond Haynes, who scored 148 in his maiden ODI innings against Australia back in 1978. Before Breetzke's innings, the highest score on ODI debut for South Africa was 124 by Colin Ingram against Zimbabwe in 2010. Now, Breetzke stands alone at the top, delivering a performance that showcased patience, aggression, and remarkable shot selection as South Africa posted a mammoth 304/6.

That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."

これらのキーが初めてSMSで使われたのはこのノキア 2110*からですが、そもそもなぜ電話機にこのような文字の割り当てがあるのでしょうか？  
それにはアメリカの歴史が関係しています！ 1950年代、ベルネットワークは電話交換手を自動化システムに置き換えました。「テキサスにつないで」のような依頼は、「839（eight three nine）」といった数字の組み合わせに置き換えられたのです。  
8…3…えっと、何だっけ？  
実はベル社には数字の扱いに課題がありました。通話の経路制御を効率よく行うために、アルファベットを数字キーに割り当てることにしたのです。使える数字は0を除いた9つ、アルファベットは26文字に対して、割り当て可能なキーは8つだけ。  
0は特別な用途で使われるため使用不可、1も何かと都合が悪い…。そうして、この数字と文字の対応表ができたのです。

src_text: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)

src_text: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."
target_text: Но самой дестабилизирующей фигурой вполне может быть жена Хуттера, Эллен, наша героиня, которая снова и снова показана телепатически настроенной на волну монстра, даже когда он находится за тысячи миль, так что полярности вроде добра и зла или желания и отвращения, кажется, просто испаряются на наших глазах. Уже один этот последний аспект, похоже, попадает в сферу интересов Роберта Эггерса. Часть подрывной энергии таких фильмов, как «Ведьма», «Маяк» и «Северянин», происходит от того, что ощущается как современный взгляд на исторических персонажей, находящихся во власти тёмных страстей, так что отдалённо историческое одновременно наделяется своей странностью и оживляется пристальной современной чувствительностью. В лучших своих моментах его версия одновременно вызывает и переосмысливает самые блестящие визуальные идеи Мурнау. Мастерское использование Мурнау непрозрачности тёмных арок, из которых может появиться вампир и в которых он может раствориться, одновременно отражается и обновляется. Знаменитое захватывающее использование Мурнау теней для визуализации оскверняющей досягаемости вампира переосмысливается, когда эти тени в новой версии простираются в 360-градусном панорамировании, вызывающем их головокружительную неизбежность. А тень руки вампира теперь простирается над всем городом, переосмысливая самый запоминающийся образ из «Фауста» Мурнау.

src_text: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.

W. ムルナウの「ノスフェラトゥ：恐怖のシンフォニー」は、それ自体がリメイクであり、ブラム・ストーカーの必読の小説「ドラキュラ」の無許可な翻案です。ムルナウと脚本家のヘンリック・ガリーンは、オリジナルの魅力的な要素を多く残しつつ、独自の大きな変更を加えました。例えば、彼らは太陽光が吸血鬼を破壊できるという、ストーカーの小説にはどこにも書かれていない伝統を確立しました。私はおそらく「ノスフェラトゥ」をあまりにも影響を受けやすい年齢で見たのでしょう。私は6歳で、PBSがそのような番組を放映しており、私のベビーシッターは私が家を燃やさないだけを喜んでいました。しかし、何度見ても私は圧倒されていただろうと思います。それはまるで墓から吹いてくる風を感じるようでした。（その影響は非常に長く、30年以上経ってから、私はこの映画とその制作に触発された小説を出版しました。）全体としては、恐怖というよりも、巧妙に不安を煽るようなものであり、そのすべてはノスフェラトゥという人物から始まりました。マックス・シュレックの演技は、102年経った今でも、邪悪で威厳のある嫌悪感の基準となっています。シュレックの吸血鬼は、悪夢の中の人物や蜘蛛の巣にいる蜘蛛のように静止しており、彼が住む世界もまた時折不安を掻き立てます。私たちのヒーロー、フッターがノスフェラトゥの城で初めて恐ろしい夜を過ごした後、彼は鏡の中で自分の首に何かが噛みついていることに気づき、微笑みます。

src_text: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."
target_text: Nejvíce destabilizující postavou však může být Hutterova manželka Ellen, naše hrdinka, která se znovu a znovu ukazuje jako telepaticky naladěná na vlnu monstra, a to i když je od něj vzdálená tisíce mil, takže polarity jako dobro a zlo nebo touha a odpor se zdají mizet, zatímco se na to díváme. Tento poslední aspekt sám o sobě by tuto historii mohl zařadit do kategorie Roberta Eggerse. Část subverzivní energie filmů jako „The Witch“, „The Lighthouse“ a „The Northman“ vychází z toho, co se zdá být moderním pohledem na historické postavy v zajetí temných vášní, takže vzdáleně historické je jak uděleno svou zvláštností, tak oživeno moderní kritickou citlivostí. V nejlepším případě jeho verze evokuje a znovu představuje Murnauovy nejbrilantnější vizuální nápady. Murnauovo mistrovské použití neprůhlednosti tmavých arkád, z nichž může vyvstat upír a do kterých se může rozplynout, je jak zopakováno, tak nově vytvořeno. Murnauovo proslulé použití stínů k vizualizaci démonického dosahu upíra je v této nové verzi znovu představeno, když se tyto stíny rozšiřují v 360stupňovém panoramatu, které evokuje jejich závratnou neodvratitelnost. src_text: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)

src_text: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)
target_text: Vždycky jsem si myslel, že jedním z nejneřešitelnějších estetických problémů je remake filmového mistrovského díla. Rozumím samozřejmě impulsu znovu se vášnivě pustit do takového díla, ale pokud je definicí mistrovského díla něco, co je jedinečné v tom, čeho se snažilo dosáhnout, jak ho můžete přetvořit, aniž byste ho jednoduše zopakovali? Existuje důvod, proč nikdo nezkusil druhou verzi Felliniho "8½" nebo Coppolova "Kmotra" nebo Polanskiho "Chinatownu"? V případě Felliniho díla někdo vytvoří ještě děsivější portrét sebeklamné toxicity mužského narcismu? V případě Coppolova díla o korozivních účincích moci? Nebo v případě Polanskiho o ničemné mužské zlomyslnosti pozdního kapitalismu? (Voda v tom filmu se nakonec ukáže jako komodita, která je manipulována pro zisk.)

src_text: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. His stunning knock of 150 off 148 balls, laced with 11 fours and five sixes, surpassed the previous record held by the legendary West Indies' batter Desmond Haynes, who scored 148 in his maiden ODI innings against Australia back in 1978. Before Breetzke's innings, the highest score on ODI debut for South Africa was 124 by Colin Ingram against Zimbabwe in 2010. Now, Breetzke stands alone at the top, delivering a performance that showcased patience, aggression, and remarkable shot selection as South Africa posted a mammoth 304/6.
target_text: Jako první hráč v historii se do rekordů zapsal jihoafrický útočník Matthew Breetzke, který v úterý v druhém zápase probíhající trojzápasové série proti Novému Zélandu na stadionu Gaddafi dosáhl 150 bodů při svém debutu v soutěži ODI. Jeho úžasný výkon 150 bodů za 148 nadhozů s 11 čtyřmi a pěti šestkami překonal předchozí rekord legendárního hráče z Indie Desmonda Haynese, který v roce 1978 dosáhl 148 bodů při svém prvním utkání ODI proti Austrálii. Před Breetzkeho výkonem byl nejvyšší bodový zisk Jihoafričanů při debutu 124 bodů, které dosáhl Colin Ingram proti Zimbabwe v roce 2010. Breetzke nyní stojí na vrcholu a předvedl výkon, který se vyznačoval trpělivostí, agresivitou a pozoruhodným výběrem úderů, když Jihoafrická republika dosáhla ohromujícího skóre 304/6.

src_text: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)
target_text: Když dojde na ty, kteří se pustili do takových hlubokých vod, někteří se pokusili o řešení „opravdu zamíchat kartami“. Existuje například politováníhodná předělávka „Kabinetu doktora Caligariho“ z roku 1962, která nejenže odstranila ústřední postavu Cesara somnambuly, ale také představila Caligariho, který místo praktikování ďábelského hypnotismu trávil čas tím, že hrdince ukazoval urážlivé obrázky. Jiní filmaři si zvolili ještě zmatenější cestu a změnili téměř nic, jako Gus Van Sant ve své téměř záběr po záběru předělávce „Psycha“ z roku 1998. Počet zklamaných diváků, které riskujete při předělávce mistrovského díla z roku 1922, je zřejmých důvodů menší, ale i tak režisér Robert Eggers v mnoha rozhovorech jasně vyjádřil své pochopení, že jeho nový „Nosferatu“ se znovu zapojuje do jednoho z největších němých filmů. (V roce 2016, když se poprvé pokusil film předělat, řekl v rozhovoru, že se cítil „ošklivě a rouhavě a egomaniacky a odporně“, že se do takového projektu pustil tak brzy ve své kariéře.)

src_text: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. His stunning knock of 150 off 148 balls, laced with 11 fours and five sixes, surpassed the previous record held by the legendary West Indies' batter Desmond Haynes, who scored 148 in his maiden ODI innings against Australia back in 1978. Before Breetzke's innings, the highest score on ODI debut for South Africa was 124 by Colin Ingram against Zimbabwe in 2010. Now, Breetzke stands alone at the top, delivering a performance that showcased patience, aggression, and remarkable shot selection as South Africa posted a mammoth 304/6.

La sua incredibile battuta di 150 run in 148 ball, con 11 quattro e cinque sei, ha superato il precedente record detenuto dal leggendario battitore delle Indie Occidentali Desmond Haynes, che segnò 148 nel suo primo innings ODI contro l'Australia nel 1978. Prima dell'innings di Breetzke, il punteggio più alto al debutto per il Sudafrica era di 124 di Colin Ingram contro lo Zimbabwe nel 2010. Ora, Breetzke è solo in cima, con una prestazione che ha mostrato pazienza, aggressività e una notevole scelta di colpi mentre il Sudafrica ha segnato un enorme 304/6.

Adding to this thread on my #Japanese #Okinawa #Rum exploration

src_text: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. His stunning knock of 150 off 148 balls, laced with 11 fours and five sixes, surpassed the previous record held by the legendary West Indies' batter Desmond Haynes, who scored 148 in his maiden ODI innings against Australia back in 1978. Before Breetzke's innings, the highest score on ODI debut for South Africa was 124 by Colin Ingram against Zimbabwe in 2010. Now, Breetzke stands alone at the top, delivering a performance that showcased patience, aggression, and remarkable shot selection as South Africa posted a mammoth 304/6.

src_text: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."

Ainuüksi see viimane aspekt paigutaks selle loo justkui Robert Eggersi pärusmaale. Osa selliste filmide nagu „The Witch“, „The Lighthouse“ ja „The Northman“ õõnestavast energiast tuleneb näiliselt kaasaegsest käsitlusest ajaloolistest tegelastest, kes on allutatud tumedate kirgede võimule, nii et kauge ajalugu saab nii tunnetatud oma võõrana kui ka elavdatud uuriva kaasaegse tundlikkuse poolt. src_text: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)
target_text: Я всегда считал, что одной из наиболее неразрешимых эстетических проблем является пересоздание выдающегося фильма. Конечно, я понимаю стремление прикоснуться к такому произведению заново с большим энтузиазмом, но если определять шедевр как нечто непревзойденное в том, чего оно пыталось достичь, как же его можно пересоздать без простого повторения? Не зря никто не пытался сделать вторую версию фильма Феллини "Восемь с половиной" или фильма Копполы "Крёстный отец" или фильма Полански "Китайский квартал". В случае с достижениями Феллини, кто сможет снять более душераздирающий портрет самообманной токсичности мужского нарциссизма? В случае с работами Копполы – разрушительного воздействия власти? Или в случае с работами Полански – о зловещем безличном насилии конца капиталистического цикла? (Например, в этом фильме вода сама по себе оказывается товаром, которым манипулируют ради выгоды.)

src_text: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)

src_text: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)
target_text: Pokud se podíváme na ty, kteří se vrhli do těchto hlubokých vod, někteří se pokusili o „skutečně rozhoupávací“ řešení. Například je tu politováníhodný remake snímku "Kabinet doktora Caligariho" z roku 1962, který nejenže vymazal klíčovou postavu somnambula Cesara, ale také představil Caligariho, který místo tím, aby praktikoval ďábelskou hypnózu, trávil čas tím, že hlavní hrdince ukazoval urážlivé fotografie. Jiní filmaři se pak vydali ještě záhadnější cestou, kdy téměř nic nezměnili, jako v případě remakeu filmu "Psycho" z roku 1998 od Gusa Van Santi. Míra nespokojenosti filmových diváků, kterou riskujete při remastingu mistrovského díla z roku 1922, je z pochopitelných důvodů nižší, ale i tak režisér Robert Eggers v mnoha rozhovorech důrazně zdůraznil své chápání toho, že jeho nový "Nosferatu" navazuje na jedno z největších děl němého filmu. (V roce 2016, kdy poprvé zkoušel tento film remastrovat, řekl v rozhovoru, že mu připadalo „ošklivé a rouhavé a egocentrické a odporné“ se do tohoto projektu pouštět tak brzy v jeho kariéře.)

src_text: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
target_text: «Носферату: Симфония ужаса» Ф. В. Мурнау сам по себе является переделкой – несанкционированной адаптацией «Дракулы», захватывающего и лихорадочного романа Брэма Стокера, – и Мурнау и сценарист Генрик Галеен сохранили многое из того, что было привлекательным в оригинале, одновременно внося свои существенные изменения: они, например, ответственны за теперь уже устоявшуюся традицию, что солнечный свет может уничтожить вампира, чего нет в книге Стокера. Вероятно, я посмотрел «Носферату» в слишком впечатлительном возрасте. Мне было 6 лет, PBS показывал подобные вещи, и моя няня просто радовалась, что я не поджигаю дом. Но я был бы потрясен, когда бы увидел его. Это было похоже на ощущение сквозняка от могилы. (Его эффект был настолько долгим, что через 30 с лишним лет я опубликовал роман, вдохновленный фильмом и его производством.) Все это было не столько пугающим, сколько коварно тревожным, и все это началось с фигуры Носферату. Игра Макса Шрека до сих пор, спустя 102 года, является эталоном зловещей и достойной отталкивающей игры. Вампир Шрека обладает неподвижностью фигуры в кошмарном сне или паука на своей паутине, и мир, в котором он обитает, порой столь же тревожен. src_text: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)
target_text: Я всегда считал, что одна из самых неразрешимых эстетических проблем — это создание ремейка киношедевра. Я, безусловно, понимаю порыв страстно взяться за переосмысление такой работы, но если шедевр по определению является чем-то непревзойдённым в том, чего он стремился достичь, как можно создать его ремейк, не скатившись в простое повторение? Не зря никто не пытался создать вторые версии «8½» Феллини, «Крёстного отца» Копполы или «Китайского квартала» Полански. В случае с достижением Феллини, сможет ли кто-то создать более мучительный портрет самообманчивой токсичности мужского нарциссизма? В случае с Копполой — разрушительного влияния власти? Или в случае с Полански — злонамеренности капитализма последней модели в духе «ничего личного»? (В этом фильме сама вода оказывается товаром, которым манипулируют ради наживы.)

src_text: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. His stunning knock of 150 off 148 balls, laced with 11 fours and five sixes, surpassed the previous record held by the legendary West Indies' batter Desmond Haynes, who scored 148 in his maiden ODI innings against Australia back in 1978. Before Breetzke's innings, the highest score on ODI debut for South Africa was 124 by Colin Ingram against Zimbabwe in 2010. Now, Breetzke stands alone at the top, delivering a performance that showcased patience, aggression, and remarkable shot selection as South Africa posted a mammoth 304/6.
target_text: Il battitore sudafricano Matthew Breetzke ha scritto la storia diventando il primo giocatore a realizzare 150 punti in una partita di debutto ODI, nella seconda sfida della tri-series in corso contro la Nuova Zelanda, allo stadio Gaddafi, lunedì. src_text: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)

Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. src_text: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.

Murnau er sjálft endurgerð - óleyfileg aðlögun á "Drakúla," ómótstæðilegri draumkenndri skáldsögu Bram Stoker - og Murnau og handritshöfundurinn Henrik Galeen héldu miklu af því sem var heillandi við frumritið á meðan þeir bættu við sínum eigin stóru breytingum: Þeir bera til dæmis ábyrgð á þeirri hefð sem nú er orðin steinrunnin að sólarljós geti eyðilagt vampíruna, hugmynd sem er hvergi að finna í bók Stoker. Ég sá líklega "Nosferatu" á of viðkvæmum aldri. Ég var 6 ára, PBS var að sýna svona hluti og barnapían mín var bara fegin að ég væri ekki að brenna húsið. En ég hefði orðið fyrir áhrifum af því í hvert skipti sem ég sá það. Það var eins og að finna fyrir drætti frá gröf. Frammistaða Max Schreck er, 102 árum síðar, enn viðmiðið fyrir ógnvekjandi og göfugan viðbjóð. Vampíra Schreck hefur kyrrð persónu í slæmum draumi eða köngulóar í vef hennar, og heimurinn sem hann býr í er stundum jafn órólegur. Eftir fyrstu ógnvekjandi nótt hetju okkar Hutter í kastala Nosferatu, tekur hann eftir því í speglinum að eitthvað hefur bitið hálsinn á honum, og hann brosir.

src_text: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)

There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)
target_text: Když se jedná o ty, kteří se do takového hlubokého rybníka pustili, někteří zkusili řešení typu „opravdové zamíchání kartami“. Například žalostné remakování „Kabinet Dr. Caligariho“ z roku 1962, které nejenže odstranilo ústřední postavu Cesareho somnambulistu, ale také představilo Caligariho, který místo praktikování ďábelského hypnotismu trávil čas tím, že hrdince ukazoval urážlivé obrázky. Jiní filmaři zvolili ještě záhadnější cestu, kdy se téměř nic nezměnilo, jako je například remake „Psycha“ z roku 1998 od Guse Van Santa, který byl téměř záběr po záběru. Počet zklamaných diváků, které riskujete při remaku mistrovského díla z roku 1922, je z pochopitelných důvodů menší, ale i tak režisér Robert Eggers v mnoha rozhovorech jasně vyjádřil své pochopení pro to, že jeho nový „Nosferatu“ znovu zapojuje jeden z největších němých filmů. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."

Часть провокационной энергии фильмов вроде «Ведма», «Маяк» и «Северянин» происходит от кажущихся современными изображениями исторических персонажей под властью темных страстей, и настолько, что историческая отдаленность как придает им незнакомые черты, так и оживляет для восприятия современных проблем. src_text: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)

src_text: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."
target_text: Nejvíce destabilizující postavou ale může být Hutterova žena Ellen, naše hrdinka, která je opakovaně ukázána jako telepaticky na stejné vlně s monstrem, i když je tisíce mil daleko, takže polarity jako dobro a zlo nebo touha a odpor se před našima očima prostě vypaří. Tento aspekt sám o sobě by mohl zařadit tento příběh do Eggersovy domény. Část podvratné energie filmů jako „Čarodějnice“, „Maják“ a „The Northman“ vychází z toho, že se zdají být moderními pohledy na historické postavy ovládané temnými vášněmi, takže vzdálená historie je zároveň zachována ve své podivnosti a oživena moderním vnímáním. V nejlepších momentech jeho verze jak evokuje, tak přetváří Murnauovy nejbrilantnější vizuální nápady. Murnauovo mistrovské využití temných oblouků, ze kterých upír vystupuje a do kterých se rozpouští, je zde jak ozvěnou, tak nově uchopeno. Murnauovo proslulé využití stínů k zobrazení upírova znesvěcujícího dosahu je přetvořeno, když se v této nové verzi stíny rozprostírají v 360stupňové panoramě, která evokuje jejich závratnou neuniknutelnost. A stín upírovy ruky se nyní táhne přes celé město, což přetváří nejpamátnější obraz z Murnauova „Fausta“.

src_text: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. His stunning knock of 150 off 148 balls, laced with 11 fours and five sixes, surpassed the previous record held by the legendary West Indies' batter Desmond Haynes, who scored 148 in his maiden ODI innings against Australia back in 1978. Before Breetzke's innings, the highest score on ODI debut for South Africa was 124 by Colin Ingram against Zimbabwe in 2010. Now, Breetzke stands alone at the top, delivering a performance that showcased patience, aggression, and remarkable shot selection as South Africa posted a mammoth 304/6.
target_text: Jihoafrický pálkař Matthew Breetzke se v pondělí na stadionu Gaddafi zapsal do historických tabulek, když se ve druhém zápase probíhající série tří zemí proti Novému Zélandu stal prvním pálkařem, který při svém debutu v ODI zaznamenal 150 runů. Svým úžasným výkonem 150 runů ze 148 míčků, který zahrnoval 11 čtyřek a pět šestek, překonal předchozí rekord legendárního západoindického pálkaře Desmonda Haynese, jenž v roce 1978 při svém prvním ODI startu proti Austrálii nasbíral 148 runů. Před Breetzkeho výkonem držel jihoafrický rekord v počtu runů při debutu v ODI Colin Ingram, který v roce 2010 proti Zimbabwe nasbíral 124. Nyní je Breetzke sám na vrcholu žebříčku a předvedl výkon, který prokázal trpělivost, agresivitu a pozoruhodný výběr úderů, což pomohlo Jihoafrice dosáhnout obrovského skóre 304/6.

src_text: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.

Ma nägin "Nosferatut" tõenäoliselt liiga muljetavaldavas eas. Olin 6-aastane, PBS näitas selliseid asju ja mu lapsehoidja oli lihtsalt õnnelik, et ma maja põlema ei pannud. Kuid see oleks mind lammutatnud ükskõik millal ma seda näinud oleksin. See oli nagu hauale tuntud õhuvool. (Selle mõjud olid nii kauakestvad, et 30 aasta pärast avaldasin romaani, mis oli inspireeritud sellest filmist ja selle valmimisest.) Kogu asi polnud niivõrd kivistav kui salakavalt rahutust tekitav, ja kõik see algas Nosferatu enda kujuga. Max Schrecki esitus on 102 aastat hiljem endiselt pahaendelise ja väärika vastikuse etalon. src_text: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
target_text: F.W. Murnau film "Nosferatu: Hõrje Sümfoonia" on ise versioon – volitamata kohandamine Bram Stokeri lugemisväärsest romaanist "Dracula" – ja Murnau ning stssenarist Henrik Galeen säilitasid palju algupärase võlu, kuid tegid samas ka suuri muutusi. Näiteks on just nemad need, kes on loonud nüüdseks kindlaks kujunenud traditsiooni, et päikesevalgus võib vampiiri hävitada, mis Stokeri raamatus ei mainita. Ilmselt nägin ma "Nosferatut" liiga noorelt. Olin kuus aastat vana, PBS näitas selliseid filme ja minu lastehoidja oli lihtsalt õnnelik, et ma ei süüdanud maja põlema. Kuid ma oleksin igas vanuses selle mõju all. See oli nagu oleksin tundnud tuulepuhangut hauale. (Selle mõju oli nii püsiv, et 30 aasta pärast avaldasin filmist ja selle tootmisest inspireeritud romaani.) Kogu film ei olnud niivõrd hirmutav kui pigem salakavalalt segastav, ja kõik algas Nosferatu enda figuurist. Max Schrecki esitus on 102 aasta möödumise järel endiselt eeskuju süngetele ja väärikatele vastikusele. Schrecki vampiiril on unenäo või ämbliku oma võrgus oleva figuuri seisak, ja tema maailm on kohati sama ebaselge. src_text: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)
target_text: Vždycky jsem si myslel, že jedním z nejzávažnějších estetických problémů je předělávka filmového mistrovského díla. Rozhodně chápu impulz vášnivě se znovu zapojit do takového díla, ale pokud je definice mistrovského díla něco, co je ve svém úsilí bezkonkurenční, jak ho předělat, aniž byste ho jen opakoval? Existuje důvod, proč se nikdo nepokusil o druhé verze Felliniho „8½“, Coppolova „Kmotra“ nebo Polanskiho „Čínského města“. V případě Felliniho díla se někdo pokusí vytvořit ještě děsivější portrét sebeklamné toxicity mužského narcismu? V případě Coppolova díla korozivních účinků moci? Nebo v případě Polanskiho díla zlovolnosti pozdního modelu kapitalismu, která není ničím osobním? (Voda samotná se v tom filmu stává komoditou, která je manipulována pro zisk.)

src_text: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."

src_text: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
target_text: Ф. В. Мурнауов „Носферату: Симфонија хорора“ је сам по себи римејк – неауторизована адаптација „Дракуле“, Брем Стокеровог компулзивно читљивог грозничавог сна о роману – а Мурнау и сценариста Хенрик Гален задржали су много тога што је било занимљиво у вези са оригиналом, док су унели своје главне измене: они су, на пример, одговорни за сада већ устаљену традицију да сунчева светлост може уништити вампира, идеја која се нигде не помиње у Стокеровој књизи. Вероватно сам гледао „Носфератуа“ у превише импресионираним годинама. Имао сам 6 година, ПБС је приказивао такве ствари и моја бебиситерка је једноставно била срећна што нисам запалио кућу. Али бих био спљоштен кад год бих га видео. Било је као да сам осетио промају из гроба. src_text: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. His stunning knock of 150 off 148 balls, laced with 11 fours and five sixes, surpassed the previous record held by the legendary West Indies' batter Desmond Haynes, who scored 148 in his maiden ODI innings against Australia back in 1978. Before Breetzke's innings, the highest score on ODI debut for South Africa was 124 by Colin Ingram against Zimbabwe in 2010. Now, Breetzke stands alone at the top, delivering a performance that showcased patience, aggression, and remarkable shot selection as South Africa posted a mammoth 304/6.

La sua straordinaria prestazione di 150 punti in 148 lanci, con 11 quattro e cinque sei, ha superato il precedente record detenuto dal leggendario battitore delle Indie Occidentali Desmond Haynes, che aveva segnato 148 punti nella sua prima partita ODI contro l'Australia nel 1978. Prima dell'innings di Breetzke, il punteggio più alto in una partita ODI di debutto per il Sudafrica era stato di 124 punti di Colin Ingram contro lo Zimbabwe nel 2010. Dne 20.06. kolem 10:30 jsem se vydal z Kolína směrem na Prahu po silnice. Po skončení úseku s kamerami v oblasti Úval, při předjíždění aut vpředu jsem překročil rychlost 90 km/h, rozumím tomu, ale nikoho jsem ne omezil a neohrožil, po předjetí jsem shodil rychlost, ale najednou v protisměru, s průsečíkem plných čar, vyjelo vozidlo na mně. Abych se vyhnul srážce, zatočil jsem doprava a pokračoval směrem k pracovníkům na dálnici. Abych se vyhnul srážce s nimi, jsem zatočil do odbočky.
Nemohl jsem moc zpomalit, protože jsem se bál silného a nekontrolovaného smyku na trávě. Z důvodu, abych zabránil vážnějším následkům, bylo mé vozidlo poškozeno a není opravitelné.. Myslím si, že poškození ve výši 180 000 Kč , zejména s ohledem na okolnosti, kdy jsem byl nucen se vyhnout jiným vážným následkům a odjet do odbočky.
target_text:
Am 20. Juni gegen 10:30 Uhr fuhr ich von Kolín Richtung Prag auf der I/12. Nach der Durchquerung eines videoüberwachten Abschnitts im Gebiet Úval überschritt ich beim Überholen kurzzeitig die zulässige Höchstgeschwindigkeit von 90 km/h. Ich bin mir dessen bewusst, möchte aber gleichzeitig betonen, dass ich niemanden gefährdet oder behindert habe. Nach dem Überholvorgang reduzierte ich meine Geschwindigkeit wieder.
Kurz darauf kam jedoch plötzlich ein entgegenkommendes Fahrzeug, das die durchgezogene Linie überquert hatte, direkt auf mich zu. Um einen Frontalzusammenstoß zu vermeiden, musste ich das Lenkrad scharf nach rechts ziehen und geriet so auf die Arbeiter am Straßenrand zu. Um auch sie nicht zu gefährden, bog ich in die Ausfahrt ein.
Ich konnte nicht stark abbremsen, da ich Angst vor einem starken und unkontrollierten Schleudern auf der Wiese hatte. Deshalb habe ich so reagiert, dass ich schlimmere Folgen vermeiden konnte. Mein Fahrzeug wurde dadurch beschädigt und kann nicht repariert werden. Ich halte den Schaden in Höhe von 180.000 CZK für akzeptabel, insbesondere unter Berücksichtigung der Umstände, unter denen ich gezwungen war, anderen schwerwiegenden Folgen auszuweichen und abzubiegen.

src_text: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)

src_text: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)

src_text: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. His stunning knock of 150 off 148 balls, laced with 11 fours and five sixes, surpassed the previous record held by the legendary West Indies' batter Desmond Haynes, who scored 148 in his maiden ODI innings against Australia back in 1978. Before Breetzke's innings, the highest score on ODI debut for South Africa was 124 by Colin Ingram against Zimbabwe in 2010. Now, Breetzke stands alone at the top, delivering a performance that showcased patience, aggression, and remarkable shot selection as South Africa posted a mammoth 304/6.

See juhtus teises kolmepoolse turniiri mängus Uus-Meremaa vastu Gaddafi staadionil esmaspäeval. Tema muljetavaldav 150 jooksu 148 pallist, milles oli 11 nelja- ja viis kuuelööki, ületas senise rekordi, mis kuulus legendaarsele Lääne-India lööjale Desmond Haynesile, kes skooris oma esimeses ODI-mängus 1978. aastal Austraalia vastu 148 jooksu. Enne Breetzke sooritust oli Lõuna-Aafrika kõrgeim tulemus ODI-debüüdil Colin Ingrami 124 jooksu Zimbabwe vastu 2010. aastal. src_text: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)
target_text: Я всегда считал, что одна из самых неразрешимых эстетических проблем – это переосмысление кинематографического шедевра. Недаром никто не пытался создавать вторые версии «8½» Феллини, «Крестного отца» Копполы или «Китайского квартала» Полански. В случае с достижением Феллини, кто-то собирается создать более душераздирающий портрет самообмана и токсичности мужского нарциссизма? В случае с Копполой – разрушительного воздействия власти? Или в случае с Полански – беспринципной злобы позднего капитализма? (В этом фильме даже вода оказывается товаром, которым манипулируют ради прибыли.)

src_text: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. His stunning knock of 150 off 148 balls, laced with 11 fours and five sixes, surpassed the previous record held by the legendary West Indies' batter Desmond Haynes, who scored 148 in his maiden ODI innings against Australia back in 1978. Before Breetzke's innings, the highest score on ODI debut for South Africa was 124 by Colin Ingram against Zimbabwe in 2010. Now, Breetzke stands alone at the top, delivering a performance that showcased patience, aggression, and remarkable shot selection as South Africa posted a mammoth 304/6.
target_text: Il giovane apertura sudafricano Matthew Breetzke si è iscritto alla storia, diventando il primo battitore a realizzare 150 corse al debutto in un incontro ODI durante la seconda partita del torneo triangolare in corso contro la Nuova Zelanda allo stadio Gaddafi, lunedì. La sua straordinaria prestazione di 150 corse in 148 palle, costellata da 11 quattro e cinque sei, ha superato il precedente record detenuto dalla leggenda delle Indie Occidentali, Desmond Haynes, che aveva segnato 148 nella sua prima partita ODI contro l'Australia nel 1978. Prima dell'innings di Breetzke, il punteggio più alto realizzato da un battitore sudafricano al debutto in un ODI era stato di 124, realizzato da Colin Ingram contro lo Zimbabwe nel 2010. Ora, Breetzke si distingue in cima alla classifica, offrendo una performance che ha dimostrato pazienza, aggressività e una notevole selezione di colpi, mentre il Sudafrica ha totalizzato un imponente 304/6.

src_text: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
target_text: F. W. Murnau „Nosferatu: Õuduse sümfoonia“ on ise uusversioon – Bram Stokeri kohutavalt kaasahaarava romaanikuju „Dracula“ loata adaptatsioon – ja Murnau ning stsenarist Henrik Galeen säilitasid palju sellest, mis oli originaalis lummav, tuues samas sisse ka omaenda olulised muudatused: näiteks nemad on vastutavad nüüdseks kivisse raiutud traditsiooni eest, et päikesevalgus võib vampiiri hävitada, mida Stokeri raamatus kusagil ei leidu. Ma nägin „Nosferatut“ ilmselt liiga emotsionaalselt haavatavas eas. Ma olin kuueaastane, PBS näitas selliseid asju ja mu lapsehoidja oli lihtsalt rõõmus, et ma maja maha ei põletanud. Aga see film oleks mind masendama surunud, ükskõik, millal ma seda ka poleks näinud. See oli nagu surnuist õhuvaipu tundmine. (Selle mõju püsis nii kaua, et kolmekümnendat eluaastat hiljem avaldasin ma sellest ja selle valmistamisest inspireeritud romaani.) Kõik see ei olnud niivõrd hirmutav kui salakavalalt häiriv ja kõik see algas Nosferatu enda figuurist. Max Schrecki näitlejatöö on ka 102 aastat hiljem endiselt kõigutamatu standard kuulutavale ja väärika välimusega vastikusele. Schrecki vampiir on paigal nagu tegelane halvas unenäos või ämblik oma võrgul, ja maailm, milles ta elab, on kohati sama häiriv. Pärast meie kangelas Hutteri esimest hirmutavat ööd Nosferatu lossis märkab ta peeglist, et miski on tema kaela hammustanud, ja ta naeratab.

src_text: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."

In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? src_text: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)

В 1962 году, например, вышел неудачный ремейк «Кабинета доктора Калигари», который не только избавился от центральной фигуры гуляющего во сне Цезаря, но и также добавил Калигари, который, вместо занятий зловещим гипнозом, тратит время показывая героине оскорбительные картинки. Другие режиссеры выбрали еще более странный путь и не поменяли почти ничего, как, например, почти полная копия «Психо» Ганса ван Санта 1998 года. Количество разочарованных зрителей в кино, которых вы рискуете получить, переделывая шедевр 1922 года, по очевидным причинам, не такое уж и большое, но даже так, режиссер Роберт Эггерс ясно дал понять в своих интервью, что понимает, что его новый «Носферату» повторяет один из величайших образцов немого кино. src_text: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
target_text: «Носферату: Симфония ужаса» режиссера Ф. В. Мурнау сам по себе является ремейком, нелегальной адаптацией «Дракулы» Брэма Стокера, которую невозможно не прочитать, а Мурнау вместе со сценаристом Хенриком Галином оставили много шокирующих деталей оригинала, при этом внеся собственные крупные правки. Они в ответе, например, за ставшую ныне классикой традицию, что вампиров может уничтожить солнечный свет, чего в книге Стокера не было. Я, наверное, посмотрел «Носферату» в слишком впечатлительном возрасте. Мне было 6 лет, по каналу PBS такое показывали, а моя няня просто радовалась, что я не спалил дом дотла. Но меня все равно бы поразил этот фильм, когда бы я его не посмотрел. Это было похоже на дуновение воздуха из склепа. (Эффект от этого настолько запомнился, что даже 30 с лишним лет спустя я написал книгу, вдохновившись фильмом и его режиссурой.) Весь фильм был не столько ужасающим, сколько жутко нервирующим, и все это началось с персонажа самого Носферату. Игра Макса Шрека, даже 102 года спустя, все еще является эталоном злодейской и гордой отвратности. Вампир в исполнении Шрека обладает спокойствием повадок, словно в кошмаре или паука в своей паутине, а мир, в котором он обитает, иногда такой же жуткий. После того, как наш герой Хаттер впервые переживает ночь в замке Носферату, он замечает в зеркале, что его укусили в шею, и улыбается.
