Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
target_text: „Nosferatu, symfonie hrůzy“ F. W. Murnaua je sám o sobě remakem – neautorizovanou adaptací „Drákuly“, horečnatého snového románu Brama Stokera, od kterého se nelze odtrhnout. Murnau a scenárista Henrik Galeen si ponechali mnohé z toho, co bylo na originálu podmanivé, a zároveň do něj vložili vlastní zásadní změny: jsou zodpovědní například za dnes již neměnnou tradici, že sluneční světlo může upíra zničit, což je myšlenka, která se ve Stokerově knize nikde nevyskytuje. „Nosferatu“ jsem pravděpodobně viděl v příliš útlém věku. Bylo mi šest, PBS takové věci vysílala a moje chůva byla prostě ráda, že jsem nepodpálil dům. Ale srazilo by mě to na kolena, kdykoli bych to viděl. Bylo to, jako bych ucítil závan z hrobu. (Jeho účinky byly tak dlouhodobé, že o nějakých 30 let později jsem vydal román inspirovaný tímto filmem a jeho natáčením.) Celé to nebylo ani tak děsivé, jako spíše zákeřně znepokojivé, a všechno to začalo samotnou postavou Nosferatu. Výkon Maxe Schrecka je i po 102 letech stále měřítkem pro zlověstnou a důstojnou odpudivost. Schreckův upír má nehybnost postavy ze zlého snu nebo pavouka v pavučině a svět, který obývá, je občas stejně znepokojivý. Poté, co náš hrdina Hutter prožije první děsivou noc na Nosferatově hradě, všimne si v zrcadle, že ho něco kouslo do krku, a usměje se.

src_text: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."
target_text: En mest óstöðvandi persónan gæti vel verið eiginkona Hutter, Ellen, aðalpersónan okkar, sem er aftur og aftur sýnd sem tengd viðskiptavinum skrímslisins, jafnvel þegar það er þúsundir mílna í burtu, svo að mótvægisafl eins og gott og illt eða ást og viðbjóð virðast bara hverfa meðan við horfum á. Sú síðastnefnda hlið gæti ein og sér komið þessari sögu í hjarta Robert Eggers. Hluti af subversífu orku mynda eins og "The Witch", "The Lighthouse" og "The Northman" stafar af því sem líkist nútímalegum túlkunum á sögupersónum sem eru í valdi myrkra ástríðna svo að hið sögulega, sem er fjarlægt, fær bæði sérstöðu sína og er blásið lífi í af nútímalegri skoðun. Í bestu mynd sinni endurvirkjar hann bæði og endurtekur bestu sjónrænu hugmyndir Murnau. Murnau's frábæra notkun á ógegnsæjum dökkum dyrum, sem vampírinn getur komið úr og leyst upp í, er bæði endurtekin og gerð ný. Murnau's fræga notkun skugga til að sjónmynda mengandi áhrif vampírsins er endurtekin þegar þeir skuggar í þessari nýju útgáfu teygja sig í 360 gráðu snúningi sem minnir á óendanlega óflótta þeirra. Og skuggi hönd vampírsins teygir sig nú yfir allan borgina, endurnýtt mynd Murnau's "Faust."

Dne 20.06. kolem 10:30 jsem se vydal z Kolína směrem na Prahu po silnice. Po skončení úseku s kamerami v oblasti Úval, při předjíždění aut vpředu jsem překročil rychlost 90 km/h, rozumím tomu, ale nikoho jsem ne omezil a neohrožil, po předjetí jsem shodil rychlost, ale najednou v protisměru, s průsečíkem plných čar, vyjelo vozidlo na mně. Abych se vyhnul srážce, zatočil jsem doprava a pokračoval směrem k pracovníkům na dálnici. Abych se vyhnul srážce s nimi, jsem zatočil do odbočky.
Nemohl jsem moc zpomalit, protože jsem se bál silného a nekontrolovaného smyku na trávě. Z důvodu, abych zabránil vážnějším následkům, bylo mé vozidlo poškozeno a není opravitelné.. Myslím si, že poškození ve výši 180 000 Kč , zejména s ohledem na okolnosti, kdy jsem byl nucen se vyhnout jiným vážným následkům a odjet do odbočky.
target_text:
Am 20.06. gegen 10:30 Uhr fuhr ich von Kolín in Richtung Prag auf der Straße. Nach dem Ende des Kameraabschnitts im Bereich von Úval überschritt ich beim Überholen der vorausfahrenden Autos die Geschwindigkeit von 90 km/h, was ich verstehe, aber ich habe niemanden behindert oder gefährdet. Nach dem Überholen reduzierte ich die Geschwindigkeit, aber plötzlich kam ein Fahrzeug aus der Gegenrichtung, mit Überschreitung der durchgezogenen Linien, auf mich zu. Um einen Zusammenstoß zu vermeiden, lenkte ich nach rechts und fuhr in Richtung der Arbeiter auf der Autobahn. Um eine Kollision mit ihnen zu vermeiden, bog ich in eine Abzweigung ab.
Ich konnte nicht stark abbremsen, da ich Angst vor einem starken und unkontrollierten Schleudern auf dem Gras hatte. Um schwerwiegendere Folgen zu verhindern, wurde mein Fahrzeug beschädigt und ist nicht reparabel. Ich denke, dass der Schaden in Höhe von 180.000 CZK, insbesondere unter Berücksichtigung der Umstände, in denen ich gezwungen war, anderen schweren Folgen auszuweichen und in die Abzweigung abzubiegen, angemessen ist.

src_text: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. His stunning knock of 150 off 148 balls, laced with 11 fours and five sixes, surpassed the previous record held by the legendary West Indies' batter Desmond Haynes, who scored 148 in his maiden ODI innings against Australia back in 1978. Before Breetzke's innings, the highest score on ODI debut for South Africa was 124 by Colin Ingram against Zimbabwe in 2010. Now, Breetzke stands alone at the top, delivering a performance that showcased patience, aggression, and remarkable shot selection as South Africa posted a mammoth 304/6.

Jeho ohromující výkon 150 bodů z 148 hodů, doplněný 11 čtyřkami a pěti šestkami, překonal předchozí rekord legendárního hráče západoindické reprezentace Desmonda Hayese, který v roce 1978 v prvním ODI zápase proti Austrálii skóroval 148 bodů. Před Breetzkeho výkonem byl nejvyšším skóre při debutu v ODI za Jižní Afriku 124 bodů Colina Inghama proti Zimbabwe v roce 2010. Nyní stojí Breetzke na vrcholu, s výkonem, který ukázal trpělivost, agresivitu a pozoruhodnou volbu úderů, když Jižní Afrika dosáhla obrovských 304/6.

src_text: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)
target_text: 我一直认为，翻拍电影杰作是当前最棘手的审美问题之一。我当然理解那种满怀热情地重塑一部杰作的冲动，但如果杰作的定义是在其所追求的成就上无与伦比，那么翻拍时又怎能避免简单的复刻呢？没人尝试翻拍费里尼的《八部半》、科波拉的《教父》或波兰斯基的《唐人街》，不是没有原因的。就费里尼的成就而言，难道会有人能对男性自恋的自欺与毒害进行更令人痛苦的描绘吗？就科波拉的作品而言，有人能更好地展现权力的腐蚀性影响吗？又或者就波兰斯基的作品而言，有人能更好地刻画晚期资本主义那种“纯属生意”的恶意吗？（在那部电影里，水本身就是被操纵以牟利的商品。）

src_text: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)
target_text: 我一直认为，重制一部电影杰作是其中一个最难以解决的美学问题。我当然理解重启这样一部作品的冲动，但如果将杰作定义为在追求目标上无与伦比的，那么你如何重制它而不只是重复它？没有人尝试过重制费里尼的《8½》或柯波拉的《教父》或波兰斯基的《唐人街》，原因就在这里。费里尼的成就，有人会制作一个更令人痛心的自我欺骗的男性自恋毒性的画像吗？柯波拉的，腐蚀性权力效应？或者波兰斯基的，后现代资本主义的无恶意的邪恶？（电影中的水本身被证明是为了利润而被操纵的商品。）

src_text: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. His stunning knock of 150 off 148 balls, laced with 11 fours and five sixes, surpassed the previous record held by the legendary West Indies' batter Desmond Haynes, who scored 148 in his maiden ODI innings against Australia back in 1978. Before Breetzke's innings, the highest score on ODI debut for South Africa was 124 by Colin Ingram against Zimbabwe in 2010. Now, Breetzke stands alone at the top, delivering a performance that showcased patience, aggression, and remarkable shot selection as South Africa posted a mammoth 304/6.

Tema uimastav löök 150-st 148 palliga, millele lisandus 11 nelja ja viis kuut, ületas eelmise rekordi, mille pidas legendaarne Lääne-India lööja Desmond Haynes, kes skooris 148 oma esimeses ODI voorus Austraalia vastu 1978. aastal. Enne Breetzke'i vooru oli Lõuna-Aafrika kõrgeim skoor ODI debüüdil 124 Colin Ingrami poolt Zimbabwe vastu 2010. aastal. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."

Podle dohod ministerstev školství a sociálních věcí by se příspěvek, který by podle poslanecké úpravy činil polovinu minimální mzdy, aktuálně zhruba 10.500 korun měsíčně, měl být začleněn do rodičovského příspěvku.
target_text: Neben dem Senat haben sich auch Bildungsminister Mikuláš Bek und die Tschechische Rektorenkonferenz gegen das Betreuungsgeld ausgesprochen. Sie kritisierten an dieser parlamentarischen Änderung des Regierungsentwurfs die Systemwidrigkeit, möglichen Missbrauch und die steigenden Ausgaben der Hochschulen, die bis zu einer Viertelmilliarde Kronen pro Jahr betragen könnten. Nach einer Vereinbarung der Ministerien für Bildung und Soziales soll die Unterstützung, die nach der parlamentarischen Änderung die Hälfte des Mindestlohns betragen würde – derzeit etwa 10.500 Kronen monatlich – in den Elternbeitrag integriert werden.

src_text: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. His stunning knock of 150 off 148 balls, laced with 11 fours and five sixes, surpassed the previous record held by the legendary West Indies' batter Desmond Haynes, who scored 148 in his maiden ODI innings against Australia back in 1978. Before Breetzke's innings, the highest score on ODI debut for South Africa was 124 by Colin Ingram against Zimbabwe in 2010. Now, Breetzke stands alone at the top, delivering a performance that showcased patience, aggression, and remarkable shot selection as South Africa posted a mammoth 304/6.

Með því að ná heilum 150 stigum úr 148 boltum, meðal annars með 11 fjörkum og fimm sexum, sló hann fyrra met kylfisins goðsagnakennda frá Vestur-Indíum, Desmond Haynes, sem skoraði 148 í fyrsta ODI-leik sínum á móti Ástralíu árið 1978. Áður en Breetzke lét til sín taka var hæsti stigafjöldinn í ODI-frumraun fyrir Suður-Afríku 124, sem Colin Ingram náði gegn Simbabve árið 2010. Nú stendur Breetzke einn á tindinum eftir frammistöðu sem bar vott um þolinmæði, kappsemi og makalaust höggval, og skilaði sér í glæsilegum úrslitum fyrir Suður-Afríku, 304/6.

Novelu, která má má především reformovat doktorandské studium včetně financování a více osamostatnit Národní akreditační úřad, nyní dostane k podpisu prezident.
target_text: Die Hochschulnovelle wird keinen Zuschuss für Studentinnen zur Betreuung ihrer kleinen Kinder einführen. Die Novelle, die in erster Linie das Promotionsstudium einschließlich der Finanzierung reformieren und das Nationale Akkreditierungsamt stärker verselbstständigen soll, wird nun dem Präsidenten zur Unterzeichnung vorgelegt.

src_text: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)
target_text: 对于那些敢于涉足这一领域的创作者来说，有些人尝试了“彻底颠覆一切”的解决方案。例如，1962年对《卡里加里博士的小屋》的可悲重拍，不仅删除了核心人物——恍惚游荡者切萨雷，还让卡里加里不再练习邪恶催眠术，而是花时间向女主角展示冒犯性的图片。其他电影制作人则选择了更令人困惑的路线，几乎不做任何改变，例如格斯·范·桑特1998年几乎逐帧重拍的《惊魂记》。重拍1922年的杰作可能会让更多观众失望，但风险较小，原因显而易见。尽管如此，导演罗伯特·埃格斯在多次采访中明确表示，他明白自己的新作《诺斯费拉图》是在重新演绎一部最伟大的无声电影。（2016年，当他第一次尝试重拍这部电影时，他告诉一位采访者，在职业生涯的早期接手这个项目感觉“丑陋、亵渎、自大且令人厌恶”。）

src_text: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)

Filmi muutmisel 1922. aastast pärit meistriteosest on tõenäoliselt vähem pettunud vaatajaid, kuid isegi see on piisavalt palju, et režissöör Robert Eggers on korduvalt intervjuudes selgitanud, et ta mõistab, et tema uus „Nosferatu“ paneb taas vaatama üht suuremaid vaikusemänge. src_text: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
target_text: F. W. Murnau „Nosferatu, õuduste sümfoonia“ on iseenesest uusversioon – loata adaptsioon Bram Stokeri vastupandamatult kaasahaaravast ja palavikulisest unenäost sündinud romaanist „Dracula“ – ning Murnau ja stsenarist Henrik Galeen säilitasid palju originaali köitvast sisust, põimides samas sisse oma olulisi muudatusi: näiteks on nemad vastutavad nüüdseks kivisse raiutud traditsiooni eest, et päikesevalgus võib vampiiri hävitada – idee, mida Stokeri raamatus ei leidu. Tõenäoliselt nägin ma „Nosferatut“ liiga vastuvõtlikus eas. Olin 6-aastane, PBS näitas selliseid asju ja mu lapsehoidja oli lihtsalt rõõmus, et ma maja maha ei põletanud. Kuid see film oleks mind jalust niitnud, olenemata sellest, millal ma seda näinud oleksin. Tundsin justkui tuuletõmbust hauast. (Selle mõju oli nii pikaajaline, et 30 ja enam aastat hiljem avaldasin romaani, mis oli inspireeritud filmist ja selle valmimisest.) Kogu asi polnud niivõrd hirmust kangestav kui hiilivalt rahutukstegev ja kõik see sai alguse Nosferatu tegelaskujust endast. Max Schrecki rollisooritus on 102 aastat hiljem endiselt pahaendelise ja väärika eemaletõukavuse etalon. Schrecki vampiiris on liikumatus, mis on omane tegelasele halvas unenäos või ämblikule oma võrgus, ja maailm, kus ta elab, on kohati samavõrd rahutukstegev. Pärast esimest hirmutavat ööd Nosferatu lossis märkab meie kangelane Hutter peeglist, et miski on teda kaelast hammustanud, ja ta naeratab.

src_text: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)
target_text: 最も解決困難な美的問題の一つは、傑作映画のリメイクだと、私は常々思ってきました。そのような作品に情熱を燃やして再び取り組みたいという衝動は確かに理解できますが、傑作の定義が、その作品が目指したものにおいて比類のないものであるならば、単なる反復にとどまらずにリメイクするにはどうすればいいのでしょうか？フェリーニの『8 1/2』、コッポラの『ゴッドファーザー』、ポランスキーの『チャイナタウン』のリメイク版が誰も試みないのには理由があります。フェリーニの偉業について言えば、男性のナルシシズムの自己欺瞞的な毒性について、これ以上に痛ましい描写をする人はいるでしょうか？コッポラの場合は、権力の腐食作用についてでしょうか？あるいはポランスキーの場合は、後期型資本主義の「何でもない個人的な悪意」についてでしょうか？（あの映画では、水そのものが利益のために操作される商品であることが判明します。）

src_text: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."
target_text: 然而，最具破坏力的人物或许就是胡特尔的妻子艾伦，她就是我们的主角，她多次显示出能够与吸血怪物产生心灵感应，而这种心灵感应距离几千英里也能产生，使得善恶或欲望与厌恶之类的概念在观众眼中仿佛突然消失了。正是这最后一点，使得这部电影似乎与罗伯特·艾格的电影如出一辙。影片如《女巫》、《灯塔》和《北海》之类电影带有的颠覆性力量，一部分来源于这些历史人物的设定被赋予了深沉的欲望，使得历史题材的作品既神秘又具有现代审美观。从最好的角度来说，这部影片既引用了又重新构想了穆瑙最精彩的视觉元素。穆瑙以过人手法运用了深暗的走廊的透明度，吸血怪物可以由此出现，亦可以从中消失。这一手法被再次运用，并赋予了新的意涵。穆瑙以令人难忘的阴影形象塑造了怪物的肮脏触手，而在这部新电影中，阴影以环形全景呈现，令人不寒而栗，仿佛这些阴影无法逃脱。此外，吸血怪手的阴影现在蔓延到整个城市，重新演绎了穆瑙的经典电影《浮士德》中最令人印象深刻的场景。

There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. src_text: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)
target_text: Vždy jsem si myslel, že jedním z nejneřešitelnějších estetických problémů je remake filmového mistrovského díla. Rozumím jistě impulzu k vášnivému opětovnému zpracování takového díla, ale pokud je definicí mistrovského díla něco bezkonkurenčního v tom, co se snažilo dosáhnout, jak ho lze remakeovat bez pouhého opakování? Existuje důvod, proč nikdo nezkusil vytvořit druhé verze Felliniho „8½“, Coppolovy „Kmotra“ nebo Polanského „Chinatown“. V případě Felliniho díla, kdo by dokázal vytvořit ještě děsivější portrét sebedestruktivní toxicity mužského narcismu? V případě Coppolovy tvorby, jakých korozivních účinků moci? Nebo v případě Polanského, jaké bezosobní zlovolnosti moderního kapitalismu? (V tomto filmu se ukazuje, že samotná voda je komoditou, která je manipulována pro zisk.)

src_text: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."
target_text:

「ウィッチ」「灯台」「ノースマン」といった映画の反逆的なエネルギーの一部は、暗い情熱に囚われた歴史上の人物に対する現代的な解釈から生まれています。そのため、遠い過去の出来事はその奇妙さを保ちつつ、現代的な視点によって活性化されます。彼のバージョンは、最高の状態で、ムルナウの最も素晴らしい視覚的アイデアを喚起し、再考します。ムルナウが暗いアーチの不透明さを巧みに使い、そこから吸血鬼が現れ、消えていく様子を描いた手法は、この新しいバージョンではエコーされ、刷新されます。ムルナウの有名な影の使い方は、吸血鬼の汚染する手を視覚化するものでしたが、この新しいバージョンでは、その影が360度のパノラマで広がり、そのめまぐるしい逃れられない様子を喚起します。そして、吸血鬼の手の影は今や都市全体に広がり、ムルナウの「ファウスト」の最も記憶に残るイメージを再利用しています。

src_text: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. His stunning knock of 150 off 148 balls, laced with 11 fours and five sixes, surpassed the previous record held by the legendary West Indies' batter Desmond Haynes, who scored 148 in his maiden ODI innings against Australia back in 1978. Before Breetzke's innings, the highest score on ODI debut for South Africa was 124 by Colin Ingram against Zimbabwe in 2010. Now, Breetzke stands alone at the top, delivering a performance that showcased patience, aggression, and remarkable shot selection as South Africa posted a mammoth 304/6.
target_text: Південноафриканський відкриваючий батер Меттью Брітцке назавжди вписав своє ім'я в історію крикету, ставши першим гравцем, який набрав 150 очок у своїй дебютній грі в ODI у другому матчі тристороннього турніру проти Нової Зеландії на стадіоні Гаддафі в понеділок. Його вражаючий результат 150 очок з 148 м'ячів, з 11 чотуками та п'ятьма шістками, перевершив попередній рекорд, який належав легендарному батеру з Вест-Індії Десмонду Хейнса, який набрав 148 очок у своїй першій грі в ODI проти Австралії в 1978 році. До виступу Брітцке найвищим результатом на дебюті в ODI для Південної Африки був 124 очок від Коліна Інграма проти Зімбабве в 2010 році. src_text: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."

src_text: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.

src_text: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.

src_text: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."

Opened this OneRum bottle intending to daiquiri, but the fragrance or lack prompted me to pull out and get nosy. Smells a bit like Indian palm toddy. Uses sugar just from Ie island. Tempted to say Clairin like but no it's more spirit, vodka or sochu like - thin, smooth with a touch of heat (48%) just a late hint it's sugar distillate. Sochu, awamori sensibilities in making it for sure. (Mizuho Distillery)
1/3
target_text:
继续分享我的日本冲绳朗姆酒探索之旅  
打开这瓶 OneRum，本想用来调制一杯代基里鸡尾酒（Daiquiri），但它的香气（或者说缺乏香气）让我忍不住仔细闻了闻。它的气味有点像印度的棕榈酒（palm toddy），只使用了来自伊江岛（Ie Island）的糖。原本以为它像 Clairin 朗姆酒，但其实它更像烈酒，类似伏特加或烧酎（sochu）——酒体轻盈、顺滑，略带辛辣感（48%酒精度），余味中才隐约显露出这是由糖蒸馏而成的酒。其酿造工艺显然融合了烧酎与冲绳传统酒“泡盛”（awamori）的精髓。（瑞穗蒸馏所，Mizuho Distillery）  
1/3

src_text: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)
target_text: 映画の傑作をリメイクすることは、最も解決困難な美学的問題の一つだと私は常々考えてきた。そのような作品に情熱的に再び取り組みたいという衝動は確かに理解できるが、傑作の定義が「その作品が成し遂げようとしたことにおいて比類のないもの」であるなら、単にそれを反復するだけでなく、どのようにしてリメイクするのだろうか。フェリーニの「8½」やコッポラの「ゴッドファーザー」、ポランスキーの「チャイナタウン」の第二版を誰も試みていない理由がここにある。フェリーニの偉業の場合、誰かが男性のナルシシズムの自己欺瞞的な毒性について、より痛烈な肖像を描くことができるだろうか。コッポラの場合は権力の腐食的影響について、あるいはポランスキーの場合は、後期資本主義の「個人的な恨みではない」悪意について。（その映画では水そのものが利益のために操作される商品であることが判明する。）

src_text: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
target_text: 弗里茨·朗（F. W. Murnau）的《吸血鬼：恐怖之交响》本身也是一部改编作品——这是一部未经授权的对布莱姆·斯托克（Bram Stoker）引人入胜的小说《德古拉》的改编——朗和编剧亨利克·加林（Henrik Galeen）保留了原作中许多精彩之处，同时又加入了一些重要的改变。例如，他们负责了现在已经成为普遍认知的传统，即阳光可以消灭吸血鬼，而这个概念在斯托克的小说中并未提及。我可能在过于年轻的年龄就看到了《吸血鬼》，当时我只有六岁，美国公共广播公司（PBS，美国公共电视网）正在播放这类影片，我的保姆只是很高兴我没有把房子烧了。但无论我什么时候看到它，都会被它深深震撼。它就像感受到了从坟墓中吹来的寒意。（它的影响如此深远，以至于三十多年后，我出版了一部受到这部电影及其制作启发的长篇小说。）整部影片并非是令人石化的恐惧，而是潜移默化的不安，而这一切都始于吸血鬼诺斯费拉图（Nosferatu）这个形象。102年过去了，马克斯·施瑞克（Max Schreck）的表演仍然是阴险而令人敬畏的恶的标杆。施瑞克的吸血鬼像噩梦中的人物或蛛网上的蜘蛛一样静止不动，而他所处的世界有时也同样令人不安。在我们的英雄胡特（Hutter）第一次在诺斯费拉图的城堡里度过可怕的夜晚后，他注意到脖子上被什么东西咬了一口，然后他露出了笑容。

src_text: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. His stunning knock of 150 off 148 balls, laced with 11 fours and five sixes, surpassed the previous record held by the legendary West Indies' batter Desmond Haynes, who scored 148 in his maiden ODI innings against Australia back in 1978. Before Breetzke's innings, the highest score on ODI debut for South Africa was 124 by Colin Ingram against Zimbabwe in 2010. Now, Breetzke stands alone at the top, delivering a performance that showcased patience, aggression, and remarkable shot selection as South Africa posted a mammoth 304/6.
target_text: Jihoafrický otevírající pálkař Matthew Breetzke se zapsal do knihy rekordů, když se stal prvním pálkařem, který dosáhl 150 běhů při debutu v ODI ve druhém zápase probíhající trojstranné série proti Novému Zélandu na stadionu Gaddafi v pondělí. Jeho úžasný výkon 150 běhů ze 148 míčů, ozdobený 11 čtyřkami a pěti šestkami, překonal předchozí rekord legendárního pálkaře Západní Indie Desmonda Haynese, který dosáhl 148 běhů ve své první ODI směně proti Austrálii v roce 1978. Před Breetzkovou směnou bylo nejvyšší skóre při ODI debutu za Jižní Afriku 124 běhů Colina Ingrama proti Zimbabwe v roce 2010. src_text: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
target_text: Фильм Ф. В. Мурнау "Носферату: Симфония ужаса" сам по себе является ремейком – неофициальной адаптацией романа "Дракула" Брэма Стокера, захватывающей и жуткой книги, – и Мурнау вместе со сценаристом Генриком Галеном сохранили многие из наиболее впечатляющих элементов оригинала, одновременно внеся в него значительные изменения: например, именно они заложили устоявшуюся традицию, согласно которой солнечный свет может уничтожить вампира, хотя в книге Стокера об этом ничего не говорится. Я, вероятно, посмотрел "Носферату" в слишком юном возрасте. Мне было 6 лет, по телевидению (PBS) показывали подобные фильмы, а моя няня была просто рада, что я не поджёг дом. Но этот фильм произвёл на меня огромное впечатление, независимо от того, когда я его смотрел. Это было как будто я почувствовал холод, исходящий из могилы. (Влияние фильма было настолько сильным, что спустя 30 с лишним лет я написал роман, вдохновлённый этим фильмом и его созданием.) Фильм был не столько пугающим, сколько жутко тревожным, и всё это началось с самого образа Носферату. Игра Макса Шрека и сегодня, спустя 102 года, является эталоном зловещей и одновременно величественной отталкивающей игры. Вампир Шрека обладает неподвижностью, как персонаж из кошмарного сна или паук в своей паутине, а мир, в котором он обитает, порой не менее тревожен. После первой страшной ночи, проведённой героем фильма, Хуттером, в замке Носферату, он замечает в зеркале, что его укусили в шею, и он улыбается.

src_text: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? Hann náði hálfri öld af 68 boltum og hélt áfram að byggja á góðri byrjun sinni, og náði að lokum sinni fyrstu öld af 128 sendingum með hjálp sex fjarka og tveggja sexa. Þar með varð hann aðeins fjórði Suður-Afríkumaðurinn til að skora öld í sínum fyrsta eins dags landsleik og slóst þannig í hóp með úrvalsleikmönnum á borð við Ingram, núverandi fyrirliða sinn Temba Bavuma og Reeza Hendricks.

src_text: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)

src_text: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
target_text: «Носферату: Симфония ужаса» Ф. В. Мурнау сам по себе является ремейком — несанкционированной адаптацией «Дракулы», лихорадочного и захватывающего романа Брэма Стокера, — и Мурнау с сценаристом Хенриком Галееном сохранили многое из того, что было притягательно в оригинале, добавив при этом свои значительные изменения: например, именно они ввели ныне незыблемую традицию, что солнечный свет может уничтожить вампира — идея, которой нет у Стокера. Вероятно, я увидел «Носферату» в слишком впечатлительном возрасте. Мне было шесть, по PBS показывали такие фильмы, а моя няня просто радовалась, что я не поджигаю дом. Но этот фильм поразил бы меня в любом возрасте. Это было похоже на дуновение из могилы. (Впечатление оказалось настолько сильным, что спустя тридцать с лишним лет я опубликовал роман, вдохновлённый этим фильмом и его созданием.) Всё происходящее на экране было не столько ужасающим, сколько коварно тревожащим, и всё это начиналось с фигуры самого Носферату. Игра Макса Шрека спустя 102 года остаётся эталоном зловещей и достойной отталкивающей силы. Вампир Шрека обладает неподвижностью фигуры из дурного сна или паука на паутине, а мир, в котором он обитает, временами столь же тревожен. После первой пугающей ночи в замке Носферату наш герой Хуттер замечает в зеркале, что у него на шее следы укуса, и улыбается.

src_text: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)
target_text: Я всегда считал, что одной из самых сложных задач в области искусства является попытка "переснять" шедевр кинематографа. Я понимаю желание вновь обратиться к такому произведению, но если под "шедевром" подразумевается нечто, что является непревзойденным в своей области, то как можно его "переснять", не ограничиваясь простым повторением? Недаром никто не пытался создать "вторые версии" таких фильмов, как "8½" Феллини, "Крёстный отец" Копполы или "Китайский квартал" Полански. В случае с фильмом Феллини, кто-то собирается создать более пронзительный портрет самообмана и токсичности, свойственных мужскому нарциссизму? В случае с фильмом Копполы – более наглядно продемонстрировать разрушительное воздействие власти? Или в случае с фильмом Полански – более ярко показать беспринципную жестокость современного капитализма? (В этом фильме даже вода оказывается товаром, которым манипулируют ради прибыли.)

src_text: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)

src_text: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
target_text: F. W. Murnauův „Nosferatu: Symfonie hrůzy“ je sám o sobě předělávkou – neoprávněnou adaptací „Draculy“, Bram Stokerova nutkavě čitelného horečnatého snu v podobě románu – a Murnau a scenárista Henrik Galeen zachovali mnoho z toho, co bylo na původním díle poutavé, zatímco vnesli své vlastní významné změny: Jsou například zodpovědní za nyní pevně zakořeněnou tradici, že sluneční světlo může upíra zničit, což je myšlenka, která se v Stokerově knize nevyskytuje. Pravděpodobně jsem „Nosferatu“ viděl v příliš dojemném věku. Bylo mi 6 let, PBS takové věci vysílala a moje chůva byla prostě ráda, že jsem nespálil dům. Ale byl bych z něj unešen, kdykoli bych ho viděl. Bylo to, jako bych cítil průvan z hrobu. (Jeho účinky byly tak dlouhodobé, že o 30 let později jsem vydal román inspirovaný filmem a jeho produkcí.) Celá věc nebyla tolik děsivá jako spíše zákeřně znepokojivá a všechno to začalo postavou samotného Nosferata. Max Schreckův výkon je i po 102 letech stále měřítkem zlověstné a důstojné odpudivosti. Schreckův upír má klid postavy ve zlém snu nebo pavouka na jeho síti a svět, ve kterém žije, je někdy stejně znepokojující. Po první děsivé noci našeho hrdiny Huttera v Nosferatově hradu si všimne v zrcadle, že ho něco kouslo do krku, a usměje se.

src_text: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.

src_text: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)

Trojcípý šátek.
Používá se k zavěšení, pokud se zlomenina nachází na horní končetině.
Při zlomenině v oblasti pánve je nutné uložit zraněného do stabilizované polohy a co nejrychleji odvézt k lékaři.
Zlomeniny se dělí na zavřené a volné.
Dlaha musí jít vždy přes dva klouby, jeden nad a jeden pod zlomeným místem.
Úlomek kosti vyčnívající z rány musí být sterilně zakryt.
Zavřená zlomenina je taková, kdy kůže nad zlomeninou není porušena.
Jako dlahu lze použít vše, co máme po ruce, např. opasek.
Při zlomenině končetiny je potřeba nejprve vrátit končetinu do původní polohy.
Pokud dojde ke zlomenině v zimě, zásadně nesundáváme oděvy, boty či rukavice, aby oteklá tkáň neomrzla.
V nouzovém případě je možné končetinu znehybnit tím, že ji přivážeme k druhé končetině.

Трикутний шарф.
Використовується для підвішування, якщо перелом знаходиться на верхній кінцівці.
При переломі в області таза необхідно покласти потерпілого у стабілізоване положення та якомога швидше відвезти до лікаря.
Переломи поділяються на закриті та відкриті.
Дуга завжди повинна проходити через два суглоби: один над і один під місцем перелому.
Уламок кістки, що виступає з рани, необхідно стерильно закрити.
Закритий перелом — це такий, при якому шкіра над переломом не пошкоджена.
Як мотузку можна використовувати все, що є під рукою, наприклад, ремінь.
При переломі кінцівки необхідно спершу повернути кінцівку в початкове положення.
Якщо перелом стався взимку, необхідно не знімати одяг, взуття чи рукавиці, щоб набрякла тканина не обморозилася.
У надзвичайному випадку можна знерухомити кінцівку, прив'язавши її до іншої кінцівки.

Dne 20.06. kolem 10:30 jsem se vydal z Kolína směrem na Prahu po silnice. Po skončení úseku s kamerami v oblasti Úval, při předjíždění aut vpředu jsem překročil rychlost 90 km/h, rozumím tomu, ale nikoho jsem ne omezil a neohrožil, po předjetí jsem shodil rychlost, ale najednou v protisměru, s průsečíkem plných čar, vyjelo vozidlo na mně. Abych se vyhnul srážce, zatočil jsem doprava a pokračoval směrem k pracovníkům na dálnici. Abych se vyhnul srážce s nimi, jsem zatočil do odbočky.
Nemohl jsem moc zpomalit, protože jsem se bál silného a nekontrolovaného smyku na trávě. Z důvodu, abych zabránil vážnějším následkům, bylo mé vozidlo poškozeno a není opravitelné.. Myslím si, že poškození ve výši 180 000 Kč , zejména s ohledem na okolnosti, kdy jsem byl nucen se vyhnout jiným vážným následkům a odjet do odbočky.

src_text: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
